extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and grant applicants (RPG mechanisms: R01/R03/R15/R21/R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard definitions and guidance for peer review of NIH Research Project Grant (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34) applications, describing the criteria reviewers should use and mechanism-specific considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15: overall impact/priority score reflects likelihood to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institution's research environment. Reviewers consider all review criteria and additional criteria when assigning the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 supports discrete, well-defined projects that can be completed in two years with limited funding; applications may not contain extensive detail or discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can be literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R15 objectives: (1) support meritorious research, (2) strengthen research environment of schools not major NIH recipients, (3) expose undergraduate/graduate students to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available. Reviewers consider whether AREA will substantially strengthen the school/academic component and expose students to research; assess investigators' experience supervising students.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel ideas or new model systems/tools/technologies with potential for significant impact; need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers focus evaluation on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Justification can be literature citations, other-source data, or investigator-generated data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials: establishing team, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, finalizing protocol, and operations manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not designed for collection of preliminary data or pilot studies. Reviewers focus on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider how successful completion will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions. For R15 also consider substantial effect on the school and exposure of students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider experience/training for Early Stage or New Investigators and record of accomplishments for established investigators. For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects assess complementary/integrated expertise, leadership approach, governance and organizational structure. For R15, also assess suitability of investigators' experience supervising students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether concepts/approaches/methodologies/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement/improvement/new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success are presented. If early-stage, will strategy establish feasibility and manage risky aspects? If human subjects/NIH-defined clinical research are involved, evaluate plans to address (1) protection of human subjects from research risks and (2) inclusion/exclusion of individuals on basis of sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and inclusion/exclusion of children, justified by scientific goals and strategy. R15 text mirrors this but specifies clinical research wording and also asks whether application provides sufficient evidence the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral sciences careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources. Determine whether the project benefits from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborations. For R15, evaluate availability of well-qualified students and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, evaluate justification for involvement and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For exempt research, evaluate: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. See 'Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects' for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, and inclusion (or exclusion) of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if inclusion/exclusion is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy. See 'Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research' for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points: (1) proposed use of animals, species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; (2) justification for use and appropriateness of species/numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort/distress/pain/injury including use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. Refer to 'Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, determine whether adequate protection (biosafety, containment, procedures) is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior comments and whether modifications address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate productivity, accomplishments, and whether the proposed renewal builds appropriately on prior progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a line of investigation from the original application not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to prior comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether foreign resources either are not readily available in the U.S. or augment existing U.S. resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided about Select Agent(s) used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) registration status of all entities where Select Agents will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer, and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing certain resources, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider the reasonableness of: (1) Data Sharing Plan, (2) Sharing Model Organisms, and (3) Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether costs and time requested align with the project's scope and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-text opportunity for reviewers to offer constructive feedback, suggestions for improvement, or strong recommendations regarding resubmission.
